correctness.rationale: The witness characteristic polynomials factor exactly as \(\chi_A(x)=x(x-6)(x-4)(x-2)(x-1)^2\) and \(\chi_B(x)=x(x-3)^2(x-2)(x^2-6x+4)\), so the Fiedler values are \(1\) and \(3-\sqrt5\). Exhaustive edge cuts give connectivities \(1\) and \(2\). All connected graph isomorphism classes through five vertices are enumerated and compared exactly within fixed \((n,m)\) layers, with no reversal.

evidence: Fiedler's full paper defines algebraic connectivity and explicitly studies its relation to usual vertex and edge connectivity; Section 4 gives inequalities connecting them.

value.rationale: Algebraic connectivity is widely used as a global network-connectivity and robustness surrogate, while edge connectivity has the direct operational meaning of the number of link failures needed for disconnection. Fixing both order and edge count makes their disagreement structurally interpretable rather than a density artifact. The minimum witness is especially informative because the spectrally preferred graph actually contains bridges while the alternative is 2-edge-connected.
